svg.title: Circuit HyperNet: from a visible failure to a learned parameter update
svg.desc: Three vertically stacked scenes. In the first, a researcher identifies Qwen's repeated output and asks a closed-weight model to investigate and edit the model. The Qwen excerpt, 'Wait, P(x) has -26.', comes from sample math_train_intermediate_algebra_738 in the MIT experiment 8 logs; TeX delimiters are omitted. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs/main/exp8_math/runs/p50c/turns/t005/prompt.txt . In the second, gibberish output and complex computation provide no clear diagnostic instruction. In the third, the circuit from the first pass is summarized as a vector and combined with the query in HyperNet. HyperNet generates a per-query LoRA for the frozen Base, trained using correct answers. These are conceptual illustrations. Highlighted features are not confirmed error-causing nodes, and the number of highlighted nodes does not measure the complexity of a failure.
